newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA UNDERLINE ONE-DAY SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA UNDERLINE ONE-DAY SUPREMACY.

text.p: Sri Lanka proved themselves worthy World Cup winners with a magnificent all-round performance on Saturday to beat Australia in the Singer World Series final.
Sri Lanka scored 234 for three then dismissed Australia -- their victims in the World Cup final in March -- for 184.
Once again, Aravinda de Silva was Australia's nemesis. He struck an undefeated 75 off 64 balls to take both the "man-of-the-match" and "player-of-the-series" awards.
De Silva's blazing innings enabled Sri Lanka to set Australia an asking rate of 6.71 runs per over. The task proved beyond them as they slumped to 48 for three.
Only Steve Waugh with a determined 55 off 53 balls and Stuart Law with 31 made any worthwhile contributions to the Australian total.
Leg-spinner Upul Chandana wrapped up the Australian innings with a spell of four for 35 in six overs.
Roshan Mahanama took a superb one-handed running catch at long-on to send back last man Glen McGrath for a duck.
But no-one could deprive de Silva of his match award. It was largely due to his spectacular batting that Sri Lanka were able to set Australia such an imposing total.
De Silva finished the tournament with an aggregate of 334 runs without being dismissed once in the four matches. He hit three sixes and two fours in his latest effort.
Earlier, Sanath Jayasuriya and Romesh Kaluwitharana set the tone for the Sri Lanka innings by scoring 42 for the first wicket off 28 balls. They made 27 and 58 respectively.
De Silva and skipper Arjuna Ranatunga finished the innings off in style with an unfinished partnership of 103 off 87 balls.
